Which of these four came first?
C++ (founded 1983) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four was released earliest?
Pascal (programming language) (published 1972) is the earliest of the four.
Pick the mathematician from these four.
Jim Simons is a mathematician. James Harris Simons (April 25, 1938 – May 10, 2024) was an American hedge fund manager, investor, mathematician, and philanthropist.
What is the atomic number of Ruthenium?
Ruthenium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ru and atomic number 44.
What is the atomic number of Chlorine?
Chlorine is a chemical element; it has symbol Cl and atomic number 17.
In what year was Marie Curie born?
Marie Curie: Curie was born in Warsaw, Russian Empire, where she studied at the clandestine Flying University and began her practical scientific training.
In what year was Nitroglycerin discovered?
Nitroglycerin: It is combined with nitrocellulose to form double-based smokeless powder, used as a propellant in artillery and firearms since the 1880s.
In what year was Thallium discovered?
Thallium is a chemical element; it has symbol Tl and atomic number 81.
Ceftriaxone: Pfizer. Ceftriaxone, sold under the brand name Rocephin, is a third-generation cephalosporin antibiotic used for the treatment of a number of bacterial infections.
In which country is Convair B-58 Hustler based?
Convair B-58 Hustler: United States. The Convair B-58 Hustler is a supersonic strategic bomber, the first capable of Mach 2 flight.
Who is credited with discovering Dubnium?
Dubnium: Joint Institute for Nuclear Research. Dubnium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Db and atomic number 105.
Who is credited with discovering Brainfuck?
Brainfuck: Urban Müller. Brainfuck is an esoteric programming language created in 1993 by Swiss student Urban Müller.
Who is credited with discovering Cobalt?
Cobalt: Georg Brandt. Cobalt is a chemical element; it has symbol Co and atomic number 27.
Home to both edible and poisonous species, this fungal genus supplies the West's most popular cultivated mushrooms, including the everyday button mushroom — which genus is it?
Agaricus is a genus of mushroom-forming fungi containing both edible and poisonous species, with over 400 members worldwide and possibly again as many disputed or newly discovered species.
Found on every continent but Antarctica and almost always monogamous breeders, which bird family unites ducks, geese, and swans under one scientific name?
Anatidae are the biological family of water birds that includes ducks, geese, and swans.
Native to Europe and Asia, which genus of burdock plants owes its seed-dispersal success to burrs that later inspired a famous fastening invention?
Arctium is a genus of biennial plants commonly known as burdock, family Asteraceae.
Created in 1989 by Brian Fox for the GNU Project as a free replacement for the Bourne shell, this command-line interpreter became the default login shell on countless Linux systems — which shell?
Bash (Unix shell) (short for "Bourne Again SHell") is an interactive command interpreter and command language developed for Unix-like operating systems.
Native to India and Nepal, this medium-sized antelope sports a striking two-tone coat, with males growing corkscrew horns up to 75 cm long. Which animal is it?
Blackbuck (Antilope cervicapra), also known as the Indian antelope, is a medium-sized antelope native to India and Nepal.
This small leafy vegetable, a cultivar of cabbage grown for its edible buds, shares its name with a European capital — what is it?
Brussels sprout is a member of the Gemmifera cultivar group of cabbages (Brassica oleracea), grown for its edible buds.

This American astronomer and planetary scientist was initially an assistant professor at Harvard before moving to Cornell as the David Duncan Professor of Astronomy. He played an active role in the Voyager programs. Who is he?
Carl Sagan (November 9, 1934 - December 20, 1996) was an American astronomer, planetary scientist and science communicator.
Patented in 1948 and used to treat hay fever and other allergic conditions, this first-generation antihistamine works within two hours by blocking the H1 histamine receptor — name the drug?
Chlorphenamine (CP, CPM), also known as chlorpheniramine, is an antihistamine used to treat the symptoms of allergic conditions such as allergic rhinitis (hay fever).

This highly venomous, nocturnal snake, black or bluish-black with narrow white crossbands, is widely distributed across South Asia, from grasslands to agricultural fields to human settlements — what snake is it?
Common krait (Bungarus caeruleus) is a highly venomous snake species belonging to the genus Bungarus in the family Elapidae.
Its name comes from the Greek for "dark blue," and its anion — a carbon triple-bonded to nitrogen — is so toxic that salts like the sodium and potassium forms cause swift poisoning. What is it?
Cyanide (from Greek kyanos 'dark blue') is an inorganic chemical compound that contains a CN functional group.
This Russian chemist's great law let him predict three undiscovered elements — germanium, gallium, and scandium — and a synthetic element now bears his name; who was he?
This Russian economist served as Vladimir Putin's economic adviser before becoming governor of her country's central bank, and was ranked among Forbes' most powerful women in 2019 — who is she?
Elvira Nabiullina (born 29 October 1963) is a Russian economist and current governor of the Central Bank of Russia.
This sensory organ detects light and converts it into electro-chemical signals in neurons, using an adjustable lens system to focus incoming light and form images — name the organ?
Eye is a sensory organ that allows an organism to perceive visual information.
He worked on uranium enrichment during the Manhattan Project, then — after McCarthyism cost him his physics post — founded San Francisco's hands-on Exploratorium museum; who was he?

Frank Oppenheimer (August 14, 1912 - February 3, 1985) was an American particle physicist, cattle rancher, professor of physics at the University of Colorado, and the founder of the Exploratorium in San Francisco.
The largest and outermost of the three hip muscles, this one shapes the buttocks and helps keep the human trunk upright — what muscle is it?
Gluteus maximus is the main extensor muscle of the hip in humans.
Though usually grouped with the birch family, some botanists split this deciduous shrub genus into its own family — and its nut is a popular snack — which plant?
Hazel are plants of the genus Corylus of deciduous trees and large shrubs native to the temperate Northern Hemisphere.
Named for a Greek youth beloved by Apollo and slain by a jealous wind god who then transformed him into this fragrant spring bloom — what flower genus is it?
Hyacinth is a genus of bulbous herbs and spring-blooming perennials.
Resembling a lump of burnt charcoal growing on birch bark, this parasitic fungus is popularly called chaga — what's its scientific name?
Inonotus obliquus (a Latinization of the Russian word), is a fungus in the family Hymenochaetaceae.
Holder of 128 firearm patents, this American engineer invented the telescoping bolt that made compact autoloading pistols possible — who is he?

John Browning (January 23, 1855 - November 26, 1926) was an American firearm designer who developed many varieties of military and civilian firearms, cartridges, and gun mechanisms, many of which are still in use around the world.
Despite its name suggesting a root vegetable, this biennial cultivar of wild cabbage grows a swollen edible stem above ground and is related to broccoli, kale, and Brussels sprouts — what is it?
Kohlrabi (scientific name Brassica oleracea Gongylodes Group), also called German turnip or turnip cabbage, is a biennial vegetable, a low, stout cultivar of wild cabbage.

Named after the Italian word for lemon, this colorless liquid hydrocarbon is the main compound behind citrus peel fragrance, occurring mostly as a right-handed form extracted commercially by centrifugal separation or steam distillation - name the compound?

Limonene is a colorless liquid aliphatic hydrocarbon classified as a cyclic monoterpene, and is the major component in the fragrance and essential oil of citrus fruit peels, taking its name from Italian limone ("lemon").
This marsupial family native to Australia and New Guinea includes kangaroos, wallabies, quokkas, and tree-kangaroos among its 63 living species — what family is it?
Macropodidae is a family of marsupials that includes kangaroos, wallabies, tree-kangaroos, wallaroos, pademelons, the quokka, and several other groups.
This nitrogen-heavy compound forms durable plastic resins used in dry-erase boards and dinnerware, and its foam version scrubs stains as the innards of a Magic Eraser — name the chemical?
Melamine is an organic compound with the formula C3H6N6.
This SI base unit for amount of substance, symbol mol, is defined so that one unit contains exactly 6.02214076×10²³ elementary entities — what is it called?
Mole (unit) (symbol mol) is a unit of measurement, the base unit in the International System of Units (SI) for amount of substance.

The first recognized fossil of this archaic human group was unearthed in 1856 in a German valley, and the species vanished around 40,000 years ago as modern humans arrived; who were these Pleistocene Europeans?

Neanderthal (nee-(r)-TAHL, nay-, -THAHL; Homo neanderthalensis or sometimes Homo sapiens neanderthalensis) are an extinct group of archaic humans who inhabited Europe and Western and Central Asia during the Middle to Late Pleistocene.

Synthesized in 2002 at a lab near Moscow and named in 2016 for the physicist who hunted down the heaviest atoms, this synthetic element claims the highest atomic number and atomic mass of anything yet known — which is it?
Oganesson is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Og and atomic number 118.
Found in organs such as the brain and lungs, inside flatworms, and within leaf cross-sections, this word names an organism's bulk functional tissue — what is it?
Parenchyma is the bulk of functional substance in an animal organ such as the brain or lungs, or a structure such as a tumour.
Made in the body from the amino acid L-phenylalanine, this natural stimulant also turns up in fermented chocolate and inhibits a transporter called VMAT2 — what is it?
Phenethylamine (PEA) is an organic compound, natural monoamine alkaloid, and trace amine, which acts as a central nervous system stimulant in humans.
It looks like a single point of light, but this brightest star of Ursa Minor is actually a triple star system parked near the north celestial pole — what is it?
Polaris is a yellow supergiant star in the northern circumpolar constellation of Ursa Minor.
This noncontagious autoimmune condition leaves dry, scaly patches of skin and can flare at the exact spot of an injury — a quirk called the Koebner phenomenon; what is it?
Psoriasis is a long-lasting, noncontagious autoimmune disease characterized by patches of abnormal skin.

This condition, often triggered by crush injuries or extreme exercise, causes skeletal muscle to break down so rapidly that it can turn urine tea-colored and damage the kidneys — what condition is it?
Rhabdomyolysis (shortened as rhabdo) is a condition in which damaged skeletal muscle breaks down rapidly.
Contracted from contaminated food, this bacterial illness typically causes diarrhea, fever, and cramps within a day or two of exposure — what is it called?
Salmonellosis is a symptomatic infection caused by bacteria of the genus Salmonella.
Cartilaginous and toothy, these fish are the sister group to the rays and skates and trace their ancestors to the Devonian Period — what are they?

Shark are a group of elasmobranch cartilaginous fishes characterized by a ribless endoskeleton, dermal denticles, five to seven gill slits on each side, and pectoral fins that are not fused to the head.
This leafy green vegetable's high oxalate content gives raw and cooked versions noticeably different flavors, with blanching helping to tone it down — what vegetable is it?
Spinach (Spinacia oleracea) is a leafy green flowering plant native to Central and Western Asia.
This South African biologist established the tiny roundworm C. elegans as a model organism, work that helped earn him a share of the 2002 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine. Who was he?
Sydney Brenner (13 January 1927 - 5 April 2019) was a South African biologist.

Beloved by biologists for its wild morphological variation and elaborate nest-building, this northern fish tolerates big swings in salinity, living in the sea but breeding in fresh water — what is it?
Three-spined stickleback (Gasterosteus aculeatus) is a fish native to most inland and coastal waters north of 30N.
These large, heavyset American game birds have a distinctive fleshy growth called a snood hanging from the base of their beak, with wild and ocellated species. What birds are they?
Turkey (bird) are large, heavyset galliforms in the genus Meleagris, indigenous to the Americas.
This pungent Japanese condiment, ground from the rhizome of a plant related to horseradish and mustard, traditionally accompanies sushi. What is it?

This teenage prodigy's work on solvable polynomials helped birth what's now called group theory, and his fiery Republican politics landed him in prison before a fatal duel ended his life at 20 — who was he?
Évariste Galois (25 October 1811 - 31 May 1832) was a French mathematician and political activist.
This practice leans on 'branding' — tying a name or image to certain qualities in people's minds — to nudge them toward buying more. What field is it?
Advertising: Form of communication for marketing.
This German polar researcher proposed in 1912 that the continents were slowly drifting apart, a theory mainstream geology only accepted decades later thanks to palaeomagnetism — who was he?
Alfred Wegener: German climatologist and geophysicist (1880–1930)
Critically endangered with barely two dozen wild individuals estimated in 2007, this big cat subspecies survives along the Russian-Chinese border in the Primorye region — which spotted predator?
Amur leopard: Subspecies of large cat. The Amur leopard (Panthera pardus orientalis) is a leopard subspecies native to the Primorye region of southeastern Russia and northern China.
This external body opening at the end of the digestive tract, positioned opposite the mouth, lets gas and solid waste pass out after digestion?
Anus: Digestive tract waste expulsion opening. Passage of feces through the anus is typically controlled by muscular sphincters, and failure to stop unwanted passages results in fecal incontinence.
Native to Eurasia, this perennial plant is grown as a vegetable crop for its tender young shoots, harvested in the spring — what's this vegetable?
Asparagus: Species of flowering plant in the family Asparagaceae.
A banana is botanically classified as which of these?
Botanically it is a berry, and the plant that bears it is not a tree but a giant herb of the genus Musa.
Produced continuously by the liver and stored in the gallbladder, this yellow-green fluid is released into the small intestine to help digest fats — what is it?
Bile: Dark greenish-brown fluid aiding in the digestion of fats.
Named for a Native American people of Oregon and Washington, this tandem-rotor heavy-lift helicopter grew out of Vertol's 1957 Model 107 design — what aircraft is it?
Boeing CH-47 Chinook: American tandem-rotor helicopter introduced in 1962 during the Cold War.
This group of roughly 20,000 non-vascular land plant species — liverworts, hornworts, and mosses — reproduces by spores instead of flowers or seeds. What is it called?
Bryophyte: Terrestrial plants that lack vascular tissue.
Once used in Italy for hunting large game and herding cattle, this mastiff breed today mostly serves as a guard dog or companion — which breed?
Cane Corso: Italian breed of mastiff. It is usually kept as a companion dog or guard dog; it may also be used to protect livestock.
Marked by patients who may lie motionless for days or repeat purposeless movements, this neuropsychiatric syndrome often responds to benzodiazepines or electroconvulsive therapy — which condition?
Native to the mountains of Honduras and Guatemala and nicknamed the 'custard apple' for its creamy texture, this fruit was called 'the most delicious fruit known to men' by Mark Twain — which fruit?
Cherimoya: Edible fruit-bearing species of plant.
This English inventor made the world's first slimline pocket calculator in 1972, then launched the UK's first mass-market home computer for under £100 — who is he?
Clive Sinclair: English entrepreneur and inventor (1940–2021)

This small, ground-nesting game bird has a call of three quick chirps repeated in succession, breeds across Europe, and winters in Africa and southern India — which species, often confused with a similar-sounding Japanese cousin?
Common quail: Species of bird. The common quail (Coturnix coturnix) or European quail is a small ground-nesting game bird in the pheasant family Phasianidae.
This interdisciplinary field draws on sociology, psychology, and law to study crime, deviant behavior, and the workings of the justice system — what is it called?
Criminology: Field of studies related to crimes.
At just 37 this American biologist won a 1975 Nobel for discovering reverse transcriptase, later running Caltech and founding the Whitehead Institute — who is he?
David Baltimore: American biologist and Nobel laureate (1938–2025)
These warmblooded reptiles ruled the land for the whole Mesozoic, and one feathered lineage of theirs survived the extinction 66 million years ago as today's birds — what group is this?
Dinosaur: Clade of reptiles. Since then, mounted fossil dinosaur skeletons have been major attractions at museums worldwide, and dinosaurs have become an enduring part of popular culture.
Also called a quake, tremor or temblor, it is the shaking of the surface caused by a sudden release of energy — in which layer of the Earth?
An earthquake is the shaking of the Earth's surface resulting from a sudden release of energy in the lithosphere that creates seismic waves.
Continuous with the outer nuclear membrane and absent from red blood cells, this organelle comes in rough and smooth forms and handles protein folding — what is it?
Endoplasmic reticulum: Cell organelle that processes proteins.
Recognizable by its striking yellow-and-azure plumage, this small European songbird nests in tree holes and can acrobatically hang upside-down from branch tips — which bird?
Eurasian blue tit: Species of bird. The Eurasian blue tit (Cyanistes caeruleus) is a small passerine bird in the tit family, Paridae.

Marketed under the brand name Captagon, this amphetamine-theophylline combination drug became Syria's largest export under the Assad regime, with tablet stockpiles seized when anti-government forces took Damascus in December 2024. What drug is this?
Fenethylline: Codrug of amphetamine and theophylline. Fenethylline (BAN, USAN) or fenetylline (INN) is a codrug of amphetamine and theophylline and so a mutual prodrug of both.
Developed by IBM with a reference manual released in 1956, this programming language became the go-to choice for numerical weather prediction and supercomputer benchmarks — what language is it?
This field studies the relationship between food and culture, encompassing everything from cooking techniques and regional cuisines to the science of good eating — what is it called?

Gastronomy: Study of the relationship between food and culture. One who is well versed in gastronomy is called a gastronome, while a gastronomist is one who unites theory and practice in the study of gastronomy.

A colorless, sweet-tasting, syrupy liquid, this sugar alcohol carries three hydroxyl groups, forms the backbone of triglycerides in fats and oils, and doubles as a food-industry sweetener. What is it?

Native to Africa and among the oldest of the chicken-like Galliformes birds, one domesticated species of this family wears a distinctive helmet-shaped casque and has been introduced worldwide — what are they?
Guinea fowl: Family of birds. Guinea fowl or guineafowl are birds of the family Numididae in the order Galliformes.
Nicknamed a 'strawberry mark' in infants, this usually benign vascular tumor tends to grow for about a year before gradually shrinking — what is it?
Hemangioma: Vascular tumor derived from blood vessel cell types.
Ashy-grey with a black head, throat and wings, this corvid was split into its own species in 2002 only to be folded back into its all-black relative by a 2025 reclassification — name the bird?
Hooded crow: Species of bird. The hooded crow (Corvus corone cornix), also colloquially called just hoodie, is a Eurasian bird subspecies of the carrion crow (Corvus corone) in the genus Corvus.

Affecting roughly one in 250 baby boys, this is the second most common birth defect of the male reproductive system, in which a key opening doesn't form in its usual place — what is this condition called?
Hypospadias: Malformation in which the urethral opening is misplaced.

Also known by names meaning 'water spinach' and 'kangkung,' this semi-aquatic tropical vegetable was likely first domesticated in Southeast Asia and thrives with barely any care near waterways — which plant is it?
Ipomoea aquatica: Species of plant. Ipomoea aquatica, commonly known as water spinach or kangkung, is a semi-aquatic, tropical plant grown as a vegetable for its tender shoots.
Once a deputy district attorney in Weld County, Colorado, this now-suspended lawyer served on Donald Trump's 2020 campaign legal team — who is she?
Native to tropical Southeast Asia, this bumpy-skinned citrus fruit is prized in regional cooking for its intensely fragrant leaves and rind, and its oil is used in perfumery — which fruit?
Kaffir lime: Citrus fruit native to tropical Southeast Asia. Citrus hystrix, called the kaffir lime, Thai lime or makrut lime, (US:, UK:) is a citrus fruit native to tropical Southeast Asia.
Sold under the brand name Lamictal, this medication treats epilepsy and helps stabilize mood in bipolar disorder — what is it?

Lamotrigine: Anticonvulsant medication. Lamotrigine ( luh-MOH-trih-jeen), sold under the brand name Lamictal among others, is a medication used to treat epilepsy and stabilize mood in bipolar disorder.

Nicknamed the 'leopard slug' for its spotted grey-brown skin, this mollusc mates by dangling from a thread of mucus off a tree branch — which species, first spotted outside Europe in Philadelphia in 1867?
Limax maximus: Species of slug. It is among the largest keeled slugs, Limax cinereoniger being the largest.
As West Germany's economics minister, he engineered the postwar 'Wirtschaftswunder' before becoming the country's second chancellor in 1963 — who is he?
Ludwig Erhard: Chancellor of West Germany from 1963 to 1966.

One of the most colorful mammals alive, this West African monkey sports vivid red-and-blue facial skin and lives in huge groups called 'hordes' — though long mistaken for a baboon, it's actually closer kin to mangabeys. What is it?
Mandrill: Species of Old World monkey from Africa.
Its name means 'big tooth,' and this extinct giant mackerel shark — once mistaken for a great white relative — is known only from fragmentary remains. What is it?
Megalodon: Extinct giant shark species. Megalodon probably had a major impact on the structure of marine communities.
Microsoft groups its proprietary operating system into families: one for personal computers, one for servers, and a third aimed at what kind of system?
Windows is grouped into families catering to particular sectors: Windows for personal computers, Windows Server for servers, and Windows IoT for embedded systems.
The platypus and the four species of echidna are the only living mammals in this order that lay eggs rather than bear live young — what is it called?

This inner-ear condition brings on episodes of vertigo, ringing in the ears, and hearing loss lasting anywhere from 20 minutes to several hours — believed to stem from fluid buildup in the labyrinth. What is it?
Ménière's disease: Disorder of the inner ear. The hearing loss and ringing in the ears can become constant over time.
This Serbian-American engineer designed the modern alternating current electricity supply system—the backbone of today's power grid. Who?
Nikola Tesla: Serbian-American engineer and inventor (1856–1943)
Starting as a metals trader after the Soviet Union's collapse, which Russian billionaire built the Sayanogorsk smelter into the world's largest aluminium company, Rusal?
Also known as jícama or Mexican turnip, this pea-family vine's edible tuberous root comes in a milky-juice form and a watery-juice form — which species is it?
Pachyrhizus erosus: Species of legume. Pachyrhizus tuberosus and Pachyrhizus ahipa are the other two cultivated species in the genus.
Derived from Greek words meaning 'healer of children,' this branch of medicine covers care from infancy through adolescence — what is it?
Pediatrics: Branch of medicine caring for children. Within the Commonwealth, pediatrics covers patients until the age of 18, except in India where the pediatric age is 12.
Formed by stripping three protons from phosphoric acid, this triply-charged ion carries the formula PO4³⁻ and lends its name to esters like trimethyl ester in organic chemistry — what anion is it?
Phosphate: Anion, salt, functional group or ester derived from a phosphoric acid.
Brightly colored as a warning sign, these diurnal tropical amphibians of Central and South America brew their toxicity from a diet of ants, mites, and termites — what's this group of frogs?
Poison dart frog: Family of amphibians.

Derived from arachidonic acid and containing a distinctive 5-carbon ring among its 20 carbons, this lipid compound can trigger opposite effects in different body tissues. What hormone-like substance is it?
Prostaglandin: Group of physiologically active lipid compounds.
Its thick bark gets harvested every 9 to 12 years for wine-bottle stoppers and cricket-ball cores — what species of oak, native to southwest Europe and Africa, is this?
Quercus suber: Species of plant. Quercus suber, commonly called the cork oak, is a medium-sized, evergreen oak tree in the section Quercus sect.

This dimensionless ratio of inertial to viscous forces predicts whether fluid flow will be smooth and laminar or chaotic and turbulent, and is used everywhere from pipe flow to aircraft wings — what is it?
Reynolds number: Ratio of inertial to viscous forces acting on a liquid.
Also called baked-apple berry or Arctic berry, this amber-hued fruit resembling a blackberry grows wild across boreal forests and Arctic tundra — what's its scientific name?
Rubus chamaemorus: Species of flowering plant in the rose family.
This large, rainbow-plumed parrot native to the forests of Central and South America is the national bird of Honduras — what is it?
Scarlet macaw: Species of bird. Like its relative the blue-and-yellow macaw, the scarlet macaw is a popular bird in aviculture as a result of its striking plumage.
The first woman on Facebook's board, she turned the company profitable as its long-serving COO and founded LeanIn.Org — who is she?
In 1948, this Japanese engineer turned a wooden shack producing bicycle motors into a multinational car and motorcycle manufacturer — who is he?
Soichiro Honda: Japanese businessman. Soichiro Honda (本田 宗一郎, Honda Sōichirō; 17 November 1906 – 5 August 1991) was a Japanese engineer and industrialist.
This English clergyman was the first person ever to measure blood pressure, and on the side he invented a ventilator and even wrote a tract against drinking — who was he?
Stephen Hales: English clergyman and scientist (1677–1761)
Derived from a Greek word meaning 'concurrence,' this medical term describes a set of signs and symptoms that tend to occur together — what is it called?
Syndrome: Association of several clinically recognizable features.
Also called oxolane, this colorless, water-miscible cyclic ether is a versatile solvent and polymer precursor — and an isomer of butanone. Abbreviated with three letters, what is it?
Discovered in Cornwall in 1791 and named after the Titans of Greek myth, this corrosion-resistant transition metal shrugs off seawater, aqua regia, and chlorine alike — what is it?
Titanium: Chemical element with atomic number 22 (Ti)

These simple-looking marine invertebrates surprise biologists: their tadpole-like larvae sport a notochord and dorsal nerve cord, making them startlingly close kin to vertebrates. What are these chordates?
Tunicate: Marine animals, subphylum of chordates.
Unlike arteries, most of these thin-walled blood vessels carry deoxygenated blood back toward the heart — what are they?
Vein: Blood vessels that carry blood towards the heart.
Fully aquatic marine mammals split into baleen and toothed kinds, their nearest land relatives are surprisingly the hippos, from which they diverged some 54 million years ago. What are they?
Whale: Informal group of large marine mammals.
As Jimmy Carter's National Security Advisor from 1977 to 1981, this Polish-American scholar organized the Trilateral Commission and oversaw normalized ties with Communist China — who was he?
Zbigniew Brzezinski: Polish-American diplomat and political scientist (1928–2017)
What is the chemical symbol for astatine?
The symbol for astatine is At. Astatine is a chemical element; it has symbol At and atomic number 85.
Rutherfordium is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for rutherfordium is Rf. Rutherfordium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Rf and atomic number 104.

Which of these is a comedian?
Peter Serafinowicz is a comedian. Peter Szymon Serafinowicz ( SERR-ə-FIN-oh-witch; Polish: [sɛrafʲiˈnɔvʲit͡ʂ]; born 10 July 1972) is an English actor, comedian and writer.
In what year was Jesse Plemons born?
Jesse Plemons (born April 2, 1988) is an American actor.
In what year was Blake Lively born?
Blake Lively: Blake Ellender Brown (born August 25, 1987), known professionally as Blake Lively, is an American actress and entrepreneur.
In what year was Pete Davidson born?
Pete Davidson: Peter Michael Davidson (born November 16, 1993) is an American comedian, actor, and writer.
In what year was Nick Jonas born?
Nick Jonas: Nicholas Jerry Jonas (born September 16, 1992) is an American singer, songwriter, musician and actor.
In what year was Reba McEntire born?
Reba McEntire: Reba Nell McEntire ( REE-bə MAK-in-tire; born March 28, 1955), or simply Reba, is an American country singer and actress.
In what year was Riley Keough born?
Riley Keough: Danielle Riley Keough ( KEE-oh; born May 29, 1989) is an American actress.
In what year was Penn Badgley born?
Penn Badgley: Penn Dayton Badgley (born November 1, 1986) is an American actor and producer.
In what year was Nicole Kidman born?
Nicole Kidman: Nicole Mary Kidman (born 20 June 1967) is an Australian-American actress and producer.
In what year was Zac Efron born?
Zac Efron: Zachary David Alexander Efron (born October 18, 1987) is an American actor.
